measures.title: Decommissioned Asset Disposition Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill makes changes to the requirements related to the decommissioning and disposal of electrical generation facilities and equipment by a project entity.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text bars a project entity from intentionally preventing the functionality of its existing coal-powered generation facility and requires it to maintain at least one operational coal unit connected to existing interconnection facilities and switchyard equipment so remaining units can be reactivated; the new Utah Energy Council exists to keep those assets generating under a competitively selected operator. A yea keeps thermal generating capacity on the grid.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Transportation, Public Utilities, Energy, and Technology Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Millner moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 70 out favorably.

measures.title: Electricity Rate Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to public utility regulation.

issues.rationale: First substitute text directs the Public Service Commission to prioritize Utah ratepayer interests when allocating utility costs, forbids recovering from Utah ratepayers the cost of facilities and programs primarily benefiting other states, and ends energy balancing account recovery for post-2024 costs. Every operative clause is about what shows up on a Utah household power bill, which is what this key measures.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Peck moved to pass H.B. 72 out favorably.

measures.title: Fluoride Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses provisions related to water fluoridation and prescription fluoride supplements.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text prohibits adding fluoride to a public water system and moves fluoride to an individually prescribed supplement a pharmacist may order. The bill replaces a population-wide, non-consensual public health dosing with per-person choice, which is the exact substance of this key: personal choice over government-administered medical treatment.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Koford moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 81 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Hinkins moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 81 out favorably.

measures.title: Vaccine Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses vaccines or vaccine material.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text designates food intended for human consumption that intentionally contains a vaccine or vaccine material as a drug, which drops it into the drug labeling and approval regime rather than the food regime. The operative effect is that no one is dosed with a vaccine through the food supply without the disclosure a drug requires.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Stratton moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 84 out favorably.

measures.title: Food Security Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill establishes a program to provide lunch at no cost to an eligible student.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text gives reduced-price-eligible students lunch at no charge, requires the State Board of Education to reimburse each LEA for those meals, bars an LEA from stigmatizing students who cannot pay, and directs meal debt communications to the parent rather than the child. This is direct household cost relief to families with children, which is what this key covers.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Defay moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 100 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Combined Basic Tax Rate Reduction
measures.generalProvisions: This bill repeals the weighted pupil unit (WPU) value rate from the combination of property tax rates that fund public education.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text repeals the weighted pupil unit value rate from the combination of statewide property tax rates levied for public education, and expressly preserves ongoing appropriations to the Teacher and Student Success Program so the repeal lands on the tax side rather than the spending side. A yea lowers the property tax a Utah owner pays.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Christofferson moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 110 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Brammer moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 110 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearm Storage Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the storage of firearms.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates a criminal penalty when an individual fails to lawfully store the individual's firearms and a minor then unlawfully accesses the firearm. A mandatory storage duty backed by criminal liability is a firearm regulation in the plain sense, and safe and secure storage is named vocabulary for this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hollins moved to pass H.B. 132 out favorably.

measures.title: Dangerous Weapons Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses statutes throughout the Utah Code dealing with dangerous weapons.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text is largely a recodification, but its substantive changes all run one way: it confirms that a person who may lawfully possess a firearm may openly carry in most public locations and conceal without a permit, removes the criminal provision for possessing a loaded rifle or shotgun in a vehicle, and repeals the crime of carrying a loaded firearm on a public street.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Strong moved to pass H.B. 133 out favorably as amended.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Thatcher moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 133 out favorably.

measures.title: Assault Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns an assault or threat of violence committed against a referee.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates an aggravating factor for assault or threat of violence committed against a referee, which raises the offense level and therefore the sentence for one class of victim. It is a sentencing enhancement and nothing else, so the link is real but narrow, which is why the weight sits at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Chair Weiler moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 140 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McKell moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 140 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearm Safety Incentives
measures.generalProvisions: This bill establishes an annual sales tax holiday for firearm safety and storage devices.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text establishes an annual week-long sales tax holiday for firearm safety devices and firearm storage devices and designates that week Firearm Safety Week. The operative mechanism is tax rather than mandate, but what it subsidizes is secure storage, which is named vocabulary for this key; the direction is toward more locked-up firearms.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McCay moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 143 out favorably.

measures.title: Rental Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts provisions related to rent increases.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires a landlord to give a tenant notice of a rent increase a set period before it takes effect. It is a tenant protection in the landlord-tenant code, giving renters time to absorb or leave ahead of an increase, which is the renter-protection half of this key rather than a funding measure.

committeeActs.committee: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Matthews moved to pass H.B. 182 out favorably.

measures.title: Sexual Offense Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill changes certain sexual offenses and sentencing for sexual offenses.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires mandatory imprisonment for repeat and habitual sex offenders, expands the child sexual abuse material definition, lowers the mental state needed for sexual exploitation of a minor, reaches accessing material with intent to view, and removes the lesser penalty tier for pubescent victims. Every change increases exposure to punishment.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Brammer moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 207 out favorably.

measures.title: Criminal Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses criminal offenses and repercussions from those offenses

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires a county sheriff and the Department of Corrections to notify and coordinate with federal immigration authorities before releasing an inmate who is unlawfully present, and adds a rebuttable presumption of flight risk in pretrial release for the same class. The state is conscripted into federal removal, which is immigration enforcement as this key defines it.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lee moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 226 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Brammer moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 226 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Balderree moved to pass 4th Substitute H.B. 226 out favorably.

measures.title: Blockchain and Digital Innovation Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates authority for the state treasurer to invest public funds in certain digital assets.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text bars state and local entities from restricting acceptance or custody of digital assets, establishes rights to run nodes, transfer assets and stake, and exempts described blockchain activity from money transmitter licensing. It is a rules-of-the-road statute for digital assets, which is the substance of this key.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Cullimore moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 230 out favorably.

measures.title: School Curriculum Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill restricts certain entities from involvement in health education in public schools.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text prohibits a local education agency from allowing an entity that performs elective abortions to provide health-related instruction or materials in a public school. The classification the statute turns on is whether the provider performs abortions, so the bill's operative distinction is abortion itself.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lisonbee moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 233 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Stratton moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 233 out favorably.

measures.title: Urban Farming Assessment Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to property tax assessment under the Urban Farming Assessment Act.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text lets land qualify for the reduced urban farming property tax assessment on gross sales as well as agricultural production, lets it keep qualifying after missing certain timing requirements, allows part of a parcel to qualify on its own, and repeals the annual renewal application. Each change makes the lower assessment easier to get and keep, which is a property tax reduction for the owner.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Watkins moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 240 out favorably.

measures.title: Statewide Online Education Program Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill makes changes to enhance quality, accountability, and transparency in the Statewide Online Education Program.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires the state board to post a report on the performance of each authorized online course provider on the Statewide Online Education Program website and adds accountability reporting for providers paid with public money. The disclosure duty is real but it is one program's provider reports, so the link sits at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Walter moved to pass H.B. 246 out favorably.

measures.title: Public Employee Gender-specific Language Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill prohibits certain employment action against a public employee in relation to gender-specific language.

issues.rationale: First substitute text bars an employer, the State Board of Education, or an LEA from disciplining an employee who refers to another individual by a name, pronoun, or other gender-specific language that conflicts with that individual's stated preference, and requires any accommodation policy to exempt the objecting employee. The protected conduct is defined by refusing a transgender person's pronouns.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Vickers moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 250 out favorably.

measures.title: State Custody Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to individuals in state custody.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text bars the state, while an individual is in state custody, from providing hormonal treatment or a surgical procedure to alter sex characteristics for the purpose of gender transition, while continuing to allow psychotherapy. The line the statute draws is transition-related medical care specifically, so the direction is on the face of the text.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hawkins moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 252 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Musselman moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 252 out favorably.

measures.title: Election Record Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to records created or used during an election.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text tightens custody and handling rules around ballots and election records and adds procedures the election officer must follow to secure them. The government records changes in the same bill cut both ways and were not given a second key; only the ballot-handling security provisions carry a single readable direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Transportation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Thurston moved to pass H.B. 263 out favorably.

measures.title: Tax Incentives Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies and repeals provisions related to income tax incentives.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text repeals the individual and corporate income tax credits for residential and commercial solar and other alternative energy systems, ending the state subsidy for customer-sited renewable generation. Removing the renewable credit is a direct reduction in state support for clean energy deployment.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Elison moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 264 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Brammer moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 264 out favorably.

measures.title: Health Curriculum and Procedures Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions regarding health instruction and physical and mental health procedures in the public education system.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires any health care provider to obtain informed parental consent before providing or facilitating telehealth or another health care service to a student inside a public school, defines restricted services and who may not provide them, and adds parental notification duties. Parental consent gates school-delivered services, which is the core of this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lisonbee moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 281 out favorably as amended.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Balderree moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 281 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Fillmore moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 281 out favorably.

measures.title: Vehicle Sales Tax Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts a sales and use tax exemption for sales of motor vehicles in separate transactions.

issues.rationale: First substitute text exempts the purchase price of the lower priced motor vehicle from sales and use tax when a person buys one vehicle and sells another in separate transactions, and sets out how to claim the exemption. It is a single new tax exemption with no offsetting increase, so the direction is a tax cut and the narrow scope is why the weight sits at the floor.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 293 out favorably.

measures.title: Amendments to Election Law
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires a voter returning a mail ballot to provide identifying digits from a state identification document and requires the election officer to verify them before the ballot counts, replacing signature comparison as the sole check. That is an identification requirement attached to casting a ballot.

A distinct provision of the same enrolled text ends universal mail balloting: beginning with the 2029 cycle a voter must opt in to receive a ballot by mail rather than being sent one automatically. That is a separate operative change from the identification requirement and it narrows how ballots reach voters, which earns its own key.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Musselman moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 300 out favorably.

measures.title: Disability Coverage Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses wraparound services for certain individuals with a disability.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text creates a state wraparound services benefit for qualified individuals with disabilities who hold minimum essential coverage other than Medicaid, with a sliding participant contribution that floors at ten percent above four hundred percent of the federal poverty level. It extends coverage for services insurance does not reach.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 310 out favorably.

measures.title: Child Tax Credit Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the individual income tax credit for child dependents.

issues.rationale: Introduced text extends the nonrefundable state child tax credit to dependents under one year old and keeps it available through age five, so a household with an infant may claim a credit it previously could not. This is per-child household tax relief, which is the substance of this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Kyle moved to pass H.B. 316 out favorably.

measures.title: Parent Access to Learning Materials Pilot Program
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates the Parent Access to Learning Materials Pilot Program.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates a three-year Parent Access to Learning Materials Pilot Program under which participating LEAs make the instructional materials used in a child's classroom available for a parent to inspect. Curriculum transparency to parents is named vocabulary for this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Peck moved to pass H.B. 325 out favorably.

measures.title: Amendments to Voting Provisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses provisions relating to voting and voter registration data.

issues.rationale: Sixth substitute text adds verification and list-maintenance duties around voter registration records and ballot handling, including checks an election officer must run before a ballot is counted. The operative provisions are about confirming eligibility and securing the count.

A distinct provision shortens the window and narrows the means by which a voter may cure or return a ballot, which is a separate operative change from the verification duties and runs against ease of casting a counted ballot. It is narrow, so it sits at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. MacPherson moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 332 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Musselman moved to pass 6th Substitute H.B. 332 out favorably.

measures.title: District Energy Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the High Cost Infrastructure Development Tax Credit Act to include district energy systems.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text adds district energy systems to the qualifying energy delivery projects eligible for the High Cost Infrastructure Development Tax Credit. It is one credit definition widened to cover shared thermal generation and distribution, so the energy-infrastructure link is real but narrow.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Koford moved to pass H.B. 350 out favorably.

measures.title: Juvenile Justice Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends statutory provisions related to juvenile justice.

issues.rationale: First substitute text restricts a minor's eligibility for a nonjudicial adjustment when the referral involves certain offenses and bars a court from granting expungement of a juvenile record if the petitioner was adjudicated or convicted of certain drug offenses within the two years before the petition. Both changes keep juvenile records and cases in the formal system longer.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Auxier moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 359 out favorably.

measures.title: Elections Office
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses issues relating to Utah's election system.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires the state board of canvassers to appoint a conflict of interest elections officer to act in place of the lieutenant governor whenever an election complaint or controversy touches a race the lieutenant governor or governor is running in, and sets that officer's term and authority. It is a conflict-of-interest cure in office administration, which is what this good-governance key covers.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Thatcher moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 369 out favorably.

measures.title: Department of Natural Resources Funding Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses revenue and expenditures related to funding state accounts within the Department of Natural Resources.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text imposes new state assessments on wind and solar electricity generation facilities, raising the cost of the two renewable sources it names and no others. The weight is held at fifty rather than higher because the receipts are directed to species protection work, so the bill is not purely a penalty on renewables.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Harper moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 378 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearm Attachment Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses firearm attachments.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates the criminal offenses of unlawful possession, manufacture, distribution, or sale of a machinegun firearm attachment, a class B misdemeanor for a first offense and a class A misdemeanor after that. A new criminal prohibition on a class of firearm hardware is a firearm restriction in the plain sense.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Carol Moss moved to pass H.B. 387 out favorably.

measures.title: Child Care Business Tax Credit
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts an income tax credit for employer-provided child care.

issues.rationale: First substitute text enacts nonrefundable corporate and individual income tax credits for employer-provided child care, subsidizing the cost of care an employer stands up or buys for its workforce. The credit exists only for child care spending, so the bill is squarely about the supply and cost of care.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Dailey-Provost moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 389 out favorably.

measures.title: Religious Expression in Higher Education
measures.generalProvisions: This bill protects student organizations' rights on a higher education campus.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text bars an institution of higher education from denying recognition, registration, or other benefits to a belief-based student organization because the organization requires its leaders or members to adhere to its sincerely held beliefs and standards of conduct. The protected act is a religious membership requirement.

A separate part of the same text limits how an institution may restrict expressive activity by student organizations on campus, which is a speech rule rather than an association-and-belief rule and therefore earns its own narrow key.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Hinkins moved to pass H.B. 390 out favorably.

measures.title: Unlicensed Driver Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses drivers without a driver license, driving privilege card, or learner permit.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text makes seizure of the vehicle mandatory rather than discretionary when an operator has no driving credential in their possession, adds driving without a credential to the impound form, requires an unlicensed driver stopped by a peace officer to present other government identification, and requires the officer to take a quick fingerprint queried against but not stored in the fingerprint system when the credential cannot be verified. Enforcement is escalated on a traffic offense, which is a narrow but single-direction link.

committeeActs.committee: House Transportation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Chair Christofferson moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 392 out favorably as amended.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Transportation, Public Utilities, Energy, and Technology Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Ipson moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 392 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Transportation, Public Utilities, Energy, and Technology Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Winterton moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 392 out favorably.

measures.title: Human Trafficking Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill increases penalties for certain human trafficking offenses.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text increases the penalties for human trafficking for sexual exploitation and related trafficking offenses, raising the offense level and therefore the sentence exposure. Nothing in the bill runs the other way; every operative change increases punishment.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hawkins moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 405 out favorably.

measures.title: School Board Referendum Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to local referendums.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text establishes a process by which voters residing in a school district may hold a local referendum on a legislative action taken by their local school board, subject to stated exceptions. It creates a ballot route that did not exist before, so the direction is toward more voting on local decisions rather than less.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Pierucci moved to pass H.B. 408 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Vickers moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 408 out favorably.

measures.title: Child Care Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to child care.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text credits time employed as a preschool teacher in a child care program toward educator relicensing and authorizes housing and transit reinvestment zone funds to be spent on constructing or expanding child care facilities inside the zone. Both changes enlarge the supply of licensed care and the workforce that staffs it.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Owens moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 410 out favorably.

measures.title: Child Custody Proceedings Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses situations related to child custody.

issues.rationale: First substitute text bars a peace officer or caseworker from taking action on the sole or partial basis that a parent asserts the gender or gender identity of the minor child is the same as the child's biological sex at birth, or does not allow, authorize, accommodate, or support a social or medical transition. The shield is defined by the parent's refusal to affirm.

A distinct provision of the same text bars action based solely on the possession or use of cannabis in a medicinal dosage form and forbids a negative inference from a parent's status as a cannabis establishment, medical cannabis pharmacy, or courier agent. That protects medical cannabis patients and workers from child-welfare consequences and is separate from the gender-identity shield.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Auxier moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 413 out favorably.

measures.title: Halogen Emissions Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses major sources of halogen emissions.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text allows the Division of Air Quality to complete a best available control technology emissions reduction plan for major halogen sources and sets the process for imposing the resulting controls. It puts a state agency to work reducing a named class of air emissions, which is the clean-air half of this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Owens moved to pass H.B. 420 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Blouin moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 420 out favorably.

measures.title: School Digital Materials Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends and enacts provisions regarding the accessibility of sensitive material through digital instructional material in a school setting.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires each LEA and school to ensure any school-provided device, database, or service a student can use runs a filter that blocks sensitive material, adds sensitive-material information to the state board parent portal, requires registration-time notice to parents and a reporting section on the LEA homepage, and lets the state board or LEA rescind a vendor contract after repeated violations. Parental notice plus material control is the substance of this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Elison moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 473 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Regulatory Oversight Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill provides additional mechanisms for the oversight of state executive agencies.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text makes the Office of Professional Licensure Review publish a form on which any person may ask that an existing occupational regulation be repealed or modified, requires that feedback in the office's report to the Business and Labor Interim Committee, and caps the cost of implementing an agency generated rule. Every operative change points at trimming existing rules.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Ipson moved to pass H.B. 474 out favorably.

measures.title: School Trespass Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions regarding criminal trespass upon school property.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text provides that public comment complying with valid time, place, manner and germaneness restrictions does not satisfy the intent element of criminal trespass, and narrows the school property to which the trespass offense applies. It removes a criminal exposure that attaches to speaking at a school board meeting, which is a speech protection, though a narrow one.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Karen Peterson moved to pass H.B. 477 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Balderree moved to pass H.B. 477 out favorably.

measures.title: Federalism Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to federalism.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text expands the Federalism Commission, raises the number of committee bill files it may open, and directs the Center for Constitutional Studies and the Herbert Institute to run federalism training for state and local employees, hold an annual federalism conference, study a state-led national federalism organization, and conduct out-of-state outreach, with executive agencies naming contacts. The bill exists to build state capacity against federal authority.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Albrecht moved to pass H.B. 488 out favorably as amended.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Vickers moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 488 out favorably.

measures.title: Judicial Retention Changes
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses judicial retention.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates a Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance that may evaluate a judge and publish a retention recommendation, requires the Judicial Performance Evaluation Commission to hand it the list of judges facing retention, requires the Judicial Conduct Committee to give it records, and puts its recommendation on the retention ballot. It is a legislative check placed directly on sitting judges.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Auxier moved to pass H.B. 512 out favorably.

measures.title: Utah Commission for Earthquake Preparedness
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates the Utah Commission for Earthquake Preparedness.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text creates the Utah Commission for Earthquake Preparedness with named membership, quorum and staffing from the Department of Natural Resources, assigns it preparedness duties, and makes its appropriations nonlapsing until a 2031 sunset. Standing state capacity for earthquake preparedness is exactly what this key measures, though a commission is a step short of a mitigation program.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Loubet moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 513 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 513 out favorably.

measures.title: Tax Payments with Precious Metals
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to tax payments.

issues.rationale: First substitute text lets severance and income taxes be paid in gold, sets a reduced severance rate for a mine operator who remits in gold, and creates an income tax credit for doing so. Making the state accept metal as payment, and paying operators to use it, is the whole bill, so a yea widens the role of specie. The reduced rate and the credit are the inducement to remit in gold rather than a tax-policy ask of their own, which is why lower_taxes is not mapped here.

committeeActs.committee: House Transportation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Vice Chair Defay moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 528 out favorably.

measures.title: Diaper Program Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses grants for entities that provide free diapering supplies to individuals.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires the Department of Health and Human Services to award grants, within appropriations, to nonprofits that give out free diapering supplies, creates the Diapering Supplies Fund, and lets individual taxpayers contribute to it on their returns. The benefit reaches households with infants as a direct material cost, which is the substance of this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Clancy moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 547 out favorably.

measures.title: Genetic Information Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the use of genetic sequencing tools and the storage of genetic sequencing data.

issues.rationale: Fourth substitute text bars a medical or genomic research facility from using a genetic sequencer or research software produced or distributed by a foreign adversary, bars storing genetic sequencing data inside a foreign adversary's boundaries or granting remote access from there without written approval, fines violations per genome, and protects an employee who reports a violation. The protected thing throughout is a person's genetic data.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Gricius moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 548 out favorably.

measures.title: Energy Corridor Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to eminent domain and the condemnation process for public utilities.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires anyone filing an eminent domain action for a high voltage power line to first complete an infrastructure siting analysis and coordinate with federal land management agencies before condemning private land, requires that documentation in the complaint, and makes the utility report annually on its eminent domain actions and use of federal public lands. It raises the bar before a private parcel can be taken.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Chew moved to pass 3rd Substitute S.B. 61 out favorably.

measures.title: Medication Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the 340B drug discount program.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text prohibits a pharmaceutical manufacturer from restricting the acquisition or delivery of 340B discounted drugs to a covered entity's contract pharmacy, and lets the Public Employees' Benefit and Insurance Program adjust practices to absorb the financial effect. Keeping the 340B discount flowing is a drug pricing measure in the plain sense.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Weiler moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 69 out favorably.

measures.title: Social Security Tax Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the individual income tax credit for social security benefits.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text raises the income thresholds at which the state income tax credit for social security benefits phases out, so more retirees keep more of the credit. The operative mechanism is a tax credit expansion with no offsetting increase anywhere in the bill, which is why this sits on the tax key rather than the benefits key.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Wilson moved to pass S.B. 71 out favorably.

measures.title: Statewide Initiatives Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to a statewide initiative.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires initiative sponsors to publish the initiative application the way a proposed constitutional amendment is published, and prohibits submitting the initiative or counting votes cast for or against it if sponsors fail to comply. A publication failure voids votes already cast, which is a restriction on a ballot route, though a narrow procedural one.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McCay moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 73 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. MacPherson moved to pass 3rd Substitute S.B. 73 out favorably.

measures.title: Mandatory Jail Sentence Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires a mandatory jail sentence for certain crimes committed under certain conditions.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires a mandatory jail sentence for certain drug and theft offenses committed under stated conditions with specified prior convictions, and provides that a person serving such a sentence may not be handed to the federal government for deportation until the full mandatory term is served. Both halves keep people in custody longer.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Musselman moved to pass 3rd Substitute S.B. 90 out favorably.

measures.title: Substance Use Disorder Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses substance use disorder screening in state correctional facilities and county jails.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires state correctional facilities and county jails to screen inmates for substance use disorders, report the screening data, and use the results in treatment and programming decisions. It builds a treatment pathway for addiction inside custody, which is named vocabulary for this key.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Thompson moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 115 out favorably.

measures.title: Landscaping Procurement Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses procurement of landscape maintenance equipment.

issues.rationale: Fourth substitute text requires a procurement unit to buy electric-powered landscape maintenance equipment when the equipment will be used primarily at a state government facility, with exemptions the facilities director may grant for terrain or emergency impracticality. It cuts small-engine emissions on state grounds only, so the link is real and narrow.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Owens moved to pass 4th Substitute S.B. 124 out favorably.

measures.title: Eviction Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses provisions relating to owners and renters.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires a new owner of a multifamily building to notify renters of the ownership change and of any rent increase of ten percent or more, lets a renter terminate an existing lease on sixty days written notice, and bars any rent increase during the new owner's first ninety days. Every operative clause is a renter protection.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 125 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearm and Firearm Accessory Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses firearms and firearm accessories.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates offenses for possessing a machinegun attachment, importing, selling, manufacturing, transferring, receiving or possessing a gas-operated semiautomatic firearm or a large capacity ammunition feeding device, adds a purchase-to-delivery waiting period, requires registration of pre-2027 covered firearms, reaches ammunition in the restricted person offense, and requires dealers to post negligent storage liability notice. The whole bill is firearm restriction.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Blouin moved to pass S.B. 130 out favorably.

measures.title: Course Choice Empowerment
measures.generalProvisions: This bill establishes a private online course choice program.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text creates an online course choice program specifically for private school students, run by an independent program manager under contract with the State Board of Education, which approves course providers, sets the payment structure, and is funded separately from public education programs. Public dollars follow a privately schooled student to a chosen course provider.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Wilson moved to pass S.B. 137 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lisonbee moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 137 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Sexual Crimes Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses sexual crimes.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text widens the definitions of child sexual abuse material and sexually explicit conduct, lowers the mental state required for sexual exploitation of a minor, reaches accessing material with intent to view, and removes the lesser penalty for material depicting a pubescent victim, with a safe harbor only for employees who must view the material at work. Every change increases exposure to punishment.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Brammer moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 144 out favorably.

measures.title: Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Adjustments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text shortens the time that must pass before an offender subject to lifetime registration may first petition for early removal from the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry, and shortens the wait before filing again after a denial. It opens an exit from a lifetime collateral consequence, which is the second-chance half of this key.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Chair Weiler moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 155 out favorably.

measures.title: Indigent Defense Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses indigent defense.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text creates the Youth Defense Fund to pay for indigent defense for a minor referred to juvenile court, has the Utah Indigent Defense Commission set the rules for county participation, and assigns administration to the Office of Indigent Defense Services. Paying for counsel a child could not otherwise afford is a due process investment on the defense side of the system.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Miller moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 171 out favorably.

measures.title: Homeless Services Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts certain provisions for individuals experiencing homelessness.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires the Department of Health and Human Services to monitor National Weather Service forecasts each summer and issue a code red alert when a HeatRisk of moderate or greater is predicted, and attaches requirements inside affected counties of the first through fourth class. The alert exists to keep unsheltered people alive through extreme weather.

committeeActs.committee: House Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Bennion moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 182 as amended out favorably.

measures.title: Tobacco and Electronic Cigarette Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to tobacco and electronic cigarette products.

issues.rationale: First substitute text adds registry and search provisions for tobacco and electronic cigarette products, creates penalties for a retailer selling flavored electronic cigarette products, raises permit fees for general retailers and specialty businesses, and amends the criminal penalties for illegal sales. Enforcement against nicotine retailers is the whole bill, and every provision tightens it, so a yea tightens the rules.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Pitcher moved to pass S.B. 186 out favorably.

measures.title: Workers' Compensation Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends the Workers' Compensation Act.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text extends the prohibition on balance billing in workers' compensation claims to health care providers and expands the Labor Commission's authority over provider fees and disclosures. Surprise billing is named vocabulary for this key, and the bill removes it for one class of patient, which is why the weight sits at the narrow-link floor.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass S.B. 190 out favorably.

measures.title: Judicial Standing Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses standing to bring a civil action.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text writes the traditional standing requirement into statute for a private right of action and finds that letting a plaintiff who lacks injury in fact, causation and redressability assert a third party's constitutional rights infringes that third party's own right to sue and conflicts with real-party-in-interest law. It narrows what a court may hear, on separation of powers grounds the text states itself.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Brammer moved to pass S.B. 203 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Musselman moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 203 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Acton moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 203 out favorably.

measures.title: Right to Appeal Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses a right to an appeal of an injunctive order.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text grants a right of appeal, and adjusts Supreme Court and Court of Appeals jurisdiction, when a trial court issues an injunctive order restraining enforcement of a state law or any part of one. It puts a single judge's injunction against a statute automatically in front of an appellate court, which is a check on that injunction power.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Brammer moved to pass S.B. 204 out favorably.

measures.title: Health Insurance Coverage Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the diagnosing of an autism spectrum disorder.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text widens the insurance code definition of a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder to include assessments, evaluations and tests performed by additional licensed professionals, so a diagnosis from those professionals triggers coverage. It is one definition, but it decides whether a family's assessment is covered at all.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 214 out favorably.

measures.title: Voter Information Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to voter registration records.

issues.rationale: Introduced text provides that when a voter whose registration record is classified as private signs a petition, that voter's name, address and other petition information may be publicly disclosed to the same extent as any other signer, with a warning printed on the petition. The private classification stops protecting the voter at the moment of signing, which is a subtraction from personal data protection.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass S.B. 218 out favorably.

measures.title: Modifications to Income Tax
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the state income tax.

issues.rationale: Introduced text imposes a separate, higher income tax rate on individual, estate and trust income above one million dollars, indexed for inflation. A new top rate is a tax increase on the face of the statute, so a yea runs against this key.

A distinct provision of the same bill makes the state earned income tax credit refundable, which puts money in the hands of low and moderate wage households rather than only zeroing their liability. That is a separate operative change from the millionaire rate and earns its own key.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass S.B. 244 out favorably.

measures.title: State Holy Days
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to certain days and commemorative periods recognized by the state.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text designates days and periods of special religious significance as state holy days, makes Easter Sunday a legal holiday, and provides that a state employee may use a personal preference day to observe a state holy day. The state is recognizing religious observance and making room for it in public employment.

committeeActs.committee: House Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Shallenberger moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 259 out favorably.

measures.title: Higher Education Certification Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates the Child Care Center Business Management Certificate Program at Utah State University.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates the Child Care Center Business Management Certificate Program at Utah State University to teach students licensing requirements and management skills for becoming a regulated provider and running a child care center, with reporting to legislative committees. It grows the provider pipeline, which is a supply measure, though one step removed from a care slot.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hayes moved to pass S.B. 264 out favorably.

measures.title: Health Insurance Preauthorization Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to health insurance preauthorization.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires health insurers to give the Department of Insurance, patients, and health care providers information about preauthorization, with a repeal date attached. Making preauthorization rules visible to the patient and the provider who must satisfy them eases access to covered care, narrowly.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McCay moved to pass S.B. 274 out favorably.

measures.title: Judicial Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to the Supreme Court.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text moves selection of the chief justice of the Utah Supreme Court from the court's own membership to appointment by the governor, subject to the advice and consent of the Senate, and reworks interim chief justice provisions. Control of the court's internal leadership passes to the political branches.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McKell moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 296 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hawkins moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 296 out favorably.

measures.title: Water Wise Landscaping Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses water wise landscaping requirements for public facilities.

issues.rationale: Introduced text imposes water wise landscaping requirements on state government facilities, defining lawn or turf and functional turf so that nonfunctional turf is limited while golf courses, parks, athletic fields and sod farms are excluded. Restricting nonfunctional turf on state property is a conservation requirement on the state's own water use.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Stratton moved to pass S.B. 305 out favorably.

measures.title: Deferred Deposit Lending Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to deferred deposit, or payday, lending.

issues.rationale: Introduced text extends the period in which a borrower may rescind a deferred deposit loan and requires the lender to give a notice of default in the language the loan was transacted in, with an English version available on request. These are consumer protections imposed on payday lenders, narrow in scope but pointed at the lender rather than the borrower.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass S.B. 329 out favorably.

measures.title: Cosmetology Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill restructures the licensing standards for the Cosmetology and Associated Professions Licensing Act.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text restructures cosmetology license classifications and qualifications and establishes approved apprenticeship standards, so an individual may qualify for licensure through a supervised apprenticeship instead of only through school hours, and exempts a registered apprentice from needing a license while training. It opens a cheaper route into a licensed trade.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass S.B. 330 out favorably.
